title: Second Largest Distinct
hints: Track the two largest **distinct** values seen so far in optionals.
When a bigger value arrives, the old largest becomes second; skip values equal to the largest.
jsBridge: In JS you'd return `undefined` or `-Infinity`. Swift returns `Int?`, so the caller is forced to handle "no answer". `Set(nums).sorted().dropLast().last` is the short version, but a one-pass scan is O(n).

compass.q: Returning `-Infinity` or `null` in JS lets callers forget the empty case. How does `Int?` make forgetting impossible?
`Set(nums).sorted()` (O(n log n)) vs one pass tracking two values (O(n)): at what size does it matter on an iPhone?
What is `[].max()` in Swift? `Math.max()` in JS returns `-Infinity`. Which is safer?
"Second best" logic shows up in leaderboards and runner-up badges. Where do ties make product decisions tricky?
